<action type="say">
Since this is a Capital One card and you can access the app, do this immediately:

1) Turn the card OFF / lock it
In the Capital One mobile app:
- Log in
- Go to “Accounts” or “Cards”
- Tap the card ending in 4419
- Look for options like:
  - “Lock Card” / “Freeze Card” / “Card on/off”
- Toggle it OFF (this blocks new transactions)

If you don’t see that:
- Look for “Need help?” / “I lost my card” / “Report card lost or stolen” on the card details page
- Follow the prompts to report it stolen — that will automatically block it

2) Officially report it stolen and request a replacement
Still in the card details:
- Tap “Settings” or the gear icon
- Look for “Replace card” / “Report lost or stolen”
- Choose “Stolen”
- Confirm your mailing address for the replacement card
- Complete the flow — they’ll give an estimated arrival date

If you can’t find it in the app, call Capital One right away:
- For credit cards, the customer service number is usually on your statement or within the app under “Contact Us”
- When you call, say: “I need to report my credit card ending in 4419 as stolen and block it immediately.”

3) Check for suspicious charges
In the app, on the same card:
- Review recent transactions (last 1–2 weeks)
- Make a list or screenshots of anything you don’t recognize (amount, date, merchant)

If you see charges you don’t recognize:
- Use the app option like “Report a Problem” or “Dispute this charge” on the transaction
- Or tell the phone agent: “These charges are fraudulent and I want to dispute them.”

4) After it’s blocked
Once the card is shut off and replacement requested:
- Turn on alerts in the app (text/push) for charges and security events
- Update any autopay services (subscriptions, utilities, etc.) once the new card arrives

Reply back once you’ve:
- Locked/reported the card in the app, and
- Either requested a replacement or spoken to an agent

Tell me what screen/options you see if you get stuck anywhere, and I’ll walk you through that exact screen.</action>
